disease.lung_cancer.name: Lung Cancer
disease.lung_cancer.description: Lung cancer is a serious disease in which abnormal cells grow uncontrollably in the lung tissue, often due to smoking or exposure to environmental toxins. It is one of the most common and deadly forms of cancer, but early diagnosis can greatly improve outcomes.
disease.multiple_sclerosis.name: Multiple Sclerosis
disease.multiple_sclerosis.description: Multiple sclerosis is a chronic autoimmune disorder that affects the central nervous system, particularly the brain and spinal cord. It can lead to symptoms such as fatigue, vision problems, difficulty walking, and muscle weakness, with severity varying between individuals.
disease.hidradenitis_suppurativa.name: Hidradenitis Suppurativa
disease.hidradenitis_suppurativa.descrip: Hidradenitis suppurativa is a long-term skin condition characterized by painful, inflamed lumps and abscesses that typically occur in areas where skin rubs together. Over time, the condition can cause scarring and tunnels under the skin, significantly affecting quality of life.

codes.legend.specialty: Specialty: Categorical coloring by medical specialty (e.g., clinical oncology). Some procedures are uncategorized and shown in white.
codes.legend.tfidf: TF-IDF (active phase 0 / 1): Importance of a code for the given label. Higher TF-IDF means the code is more specific to the label.
codes.legend.frequency: Frequency: Based on total occurrence of the code across all sequences. More frequent codes are darker.

models.metrics.accuracy.tooltip: Percentage of all predictions — both positive and negative — that are correct. Can be misleading when one class is much more common than the other.
models.metrics.precision.tooltip: When the model raises an alert, how often it is actually correct. High precision means fewer unnecessary follow-ups.
models.metrics.recall.tooltip: How many of the real positive cases the model successfully catches. High recall means fewer missed diagnoses.
models.metrics.f1.tooltip: A single score that balances precision and recall. Useful when you care equally about catching cases and avoiding false alarms.
models.metrics.roc_auc.tooltip: How well the model separates positive from negative cases across all possible thresholds. 1.0 is perfect, 0.5 is no better than random guessing.
